This product covers Southeast Texas

**Bertha Weakens to a Depression, All Tropical Storm Warnings are Cancelled**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- All watches and warnings have been canceled

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

through southeast Texas. Bertha will continue to weaken, becoming a

and southwest of the center. No other significant impacts are expected
as winds continue to subside.

-----------------

western Houston metro and Brazos Valley. Remain well guarded against
locally hazardous flood waters having further impacts of limited
potential.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Be alert for flooded roads. Do not drive through places where flood
waters cover the road. Turn around, don't drown!

- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

issued by the National Weather Service in Houston/Galveston TX
regarding the effects of tropical cyclone hazards upon the area.

alerts.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 23 at 5:08PM CDT until July 23 at 8:15PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Urban and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Texas, including the following
counties, Brazoria, Fort Bend and Harris.

* WHEN...Until 815 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Ponding of water in urban or other areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 508 PM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated heavy rain due to thunderstorms. This is causing
urban and small stream flooding. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches
of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Pearland, Sugar Land, Missouri City, eastern Rosenberg,
Stafford, South Houston, Bellaire, West University Place,
Richmond, northwestern Manvel, Fresno, First Colony, Town
West, Astrodome Area, University Place, Mission Bend,
Macgregor, Pecan Grove, Greater Hobby Area and western South
Belt / Ellington.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

**Bertha expected to weaken as it moves through Southeast Texas**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Bolivar Peninsula,
Brazoria Islands, Chambers, Coastal Brazoria, Coastal
Galveston, and Galveston Island

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 40 miles north of Galveston TX
- 29.8N 94.7W
- Storm Intensity 40 mph
- Movement West-northwest or 290 degrees at 13 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Bertha is currently moving westward through southeast
Texas, roughtly around the I-10 corridor nearly Galveston bay. It's
intensity has decreased, with peak winds upwards of 35 knots. Bertha
will continue to weaken, becoming a post-tropical system as it moves
westward tonight. No significant impacts to Southeast Texas are
expected at this time. Winds of 15-25 knots with gusts to 35 knots will
be possible, mainly along the coast and Gulf waters. Scattered showers
and thunderstorms continue this evening. Heavy downpours are possible
though the flooding rain threat is very low. A high risk rip currents
will continue across the beaches and coast through Friday.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
Southeast Texas. Remain well sheltered from hazardous wind having
possible limited impacts. If realized, these impacts
include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across
the Southeast Texas coast. Remain well guarded against locally
hazardous flood waters having possible  limited
impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Localized rainfall flooding may prompt a few evacuations.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly rise with swifter currents.
Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may become swollen
and overflow in spots.
- Flood waters can enter a few structures, especially in usually
vulnerable spots. A few places where rapid ponding of water
occurs at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Several storm drains and retention ponds become
near-full and begin to overflow. Some brief road and bridge
closures.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* OTHER COASTAL HAZARDS:
There will be a high risk of rip currents across the upper Texas
coastal beaches through Friday.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Keep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose
power, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and
check-ins.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Houston/Galveston TX around 7 PM CDT, or sooner if
conditions warrant.

This product covers Southeast Texas

**Bertha Weakens to a Depression, All Tropical Storm Warnings are Cancelled**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- All watches and warnings have been canceled

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 20 miles north-northeast of Houston TX
- 29.9N 95.3W
- Storm Intensity 35 mph
- Movement West or 280 degrees at 13 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Depression Bertha continues to weaken as it moves westward
through southeast Texas. Bertha will continue to weaken, becoming a
post-tropical system as it moves westward tonight. Locally heavy
downpours remain possible for the next few hours mainly to the south
and southwest of the center. No other significant impacts are expected
as winds continue to subside.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Additional impacts from flooding rain are still a concern across the
western Houston metro and Brazos Valley. Remain well guarded against
locally hazardous flood waters having further impacts of limited
potential.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Be alert for flooded roads. Do not drive through places where flood
waters cover the road. Turn around, don't drown!

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

As it pertains to this event...this will be the last local statement
issued by the National Weather Service in Houston/Galveston TX
regarding the effects of tropical cyclone hazards upon the area.

This product covers Southeast Texas

**Bertha expected to weaken as it moves through Southeast Texas**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Bolivar Peninsula,
Brazoria Islands, Chambers, Coastal Brazoria, Coastal
Galveston, and Galveston Island

- About 40 miles north of Galveston TX
- 29.8N 94.7W
- Storm Intensity 40 mph
- Movement West-northwest or 290 degrees at 13 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Bertha is currently moving westward through southeast
Texas, roughtly around the I-10 corridor nearly Galveston bay. It's
intensity has decreased, with peak winds upwards of 35 knots. Bertha
will continue to weaken, becoming a post-tropical system as it moves
westward tonight. No significant impacts to Southeast Texas are
expected at this time. Winds of 15-25 knots with gusts to 35 knots will
be possible, mainly along the coast and Gulf waters. Scattered showers
and thunderstorms continue this evening. Heavy downpours are possible
though the flooding rain threat is very low. A high risk rip currents
will continue across the beaches and coast through Friday.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
Southeast Texas. Remain well sheltered from hazardous wind having
possible limited impacts. If realized, these impacts
include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across
the Southeast Texas coast. Remain well guarded against locally
hazardous flood waters having possible  limited
impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Localized rainfall flooding may prompt a few evacuations.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly rise with swifter currents.
Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may become swollen
and overflow in spots.
- Flood waters can enter a few structures, especially in usually
vulnerable spots. A few places where rapid ponding of water
occurs at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Several storm drains and retention ponds become
near-full and begin to overflow. Some brief road and bridge
closures.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* OTHER COASTAL HAZARDS:
There will be a high risk of rip currents across the upper Texas
coastal beaches through Friday.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Keep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose
power, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and
check-ins.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Houston/Galveston TX around 7 PM CDT, or sooner if
conditions warrant.

HLSLCH

This product covers Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas

**TROPICAL STORM BERTHA HAS MOVED INLAND INTO SOUTHEASTERN TEXAS.**


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- The Tropical Storm Warning has been cancelled for Lower Iberia,
Lower St. Mary, and Lower Vermilion

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for East Cameron, Lower
Jefferson, and West Cameron

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 30 miles northwest of High Island TX or about 80 miles
west of Cameron LA
- 29.8N 94.7W
- Storm Intensity 40 mph
- Movement West-northwest or 290 degrees at 13 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Bertha has moved inland over lower Southeast Texas
continuing a weakening trend. Tropical storm warnings have been
discontinued east of the Cameron / Vermilion Parish line as well as
marine south extending south and east of Calcasieu Pass. Tropical
Storm Warnings remain in effect across western Cameron Parish,
Louisiana, and Jefferson County, Texas including Calcasieu and Sabine
Lakes. The remainder of the forecast remains unchanged with 1 to
2 feet of surge possible and most of the heavy rainfall remaining
offshore due to the sheared nature of the convection. Bertha is
expected to weaken into a tropical depression overnight as it
encounters more land interaction moving further into Texas.


POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
Southwest Louisiana / Southeast Texas. Remain well sheltered from hazardous
wind having limited impacts. If realized,
these impacts include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Potential impacts from the main surge event are now unfolding across
Southwest Louisiana / Southeast Texas. Remain well away from locally hazardous
surge having limited impacts. If
realized, these impacts include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time
across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas.

* TORNADOES:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time
across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:

Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Now is the time to stay inside and away from windows. Listen for
updates and be ready in case you lose electrical power. Keep a
battery-powered radio, charged cell phone and flashlight handy.

During the peak of the storm be ready to move quickly. Keep your
shoes on and rain gear handy. Boots and athletic shoes offer the best
foot protection if you become unexpectedly exposed to the weather.

Keep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose
power, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and
check-ins.



* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Lake Charles LA around 10 PM CDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

alerts.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued July 23 at 6:51PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
alerts.description:
HLSHGX

This product covers Southeast Texas

**Bertha Weakens to a Depression, All Tropical Storm Warnings are Cancelled**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- All watches and warnings have been canceled

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 20 miles north-northeast of Houston TX
- 29.9N 95.3W
- Storm Intensity 35 mph
- Movement West or 280 degrees at 13 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Depression Bertha continues to weaken as it moves westward
through southeast Texas. Bertha will continue to weaken, becoming a
post-tropical system as it moves westward tonight. Locally heavy
downpours remain possible for the next few hours mainly to the south
and southwest of the center. No other significant impacts are expected
as winds continue to subside.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Additional impacts from flooding rain are still a concern across the
western Houston metro and Brazos Valley. Remain well guarded against
locally hazardous flood waters having further impacts of limited
potential.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Be alert for flooded roads. Do not drive through places where flood
waters cover the road. Turn around, don't drown!

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

As it pertains to this event...this will be the last local statement
issued by the National Weather Service in Houston/Galveston TX
regarding the effects of tropical cyclone hazards upon the area.

alerts.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued July 23 at 4:15PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
alerts.description:
HLSHGX

This product covers Southeast Texas

**Bertha expected to weaken as it moves through Southeast Texas**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Bolivar Peninsula,
Brazoria Islands, Chambers, Coastal Brazoria, Coastal
Galveston, and Galveston Island

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 40 miles north of Galveston TX
- 29.8N 94.7W
- Storm Intensity 40 mph
- Movement West-northwest or 290 degrees at 13 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Bertha is currently moving westward through southeast
Texas, roughtly around the I-10 corridor nearly Galveston bay. It's
intensity has decreased, with peak winds upwards of 35 knots. Bertha
will continue to weaken, becoming a post-tropical system as it moves
westward tonight. No significant impacts to Southeast Texas are
expected at this time. Winds of 15-25 knots with gusts to 35 knots will
be possible, mainly along the coast and Gulf waters. Scattered showers
and thunderstorms continue this evening. Heavy downpours are possible
though the flooding rain threat is very low. A high risk rip currents
will continue across the beaches and coast through Friday.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
Southeast Texas. Remain well sheltered from hazardous wind having
possible limited impacts. If realized, these impacts
include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across
the Southeast Texas coast. Remain well guarded against locally
hazardous flood waters having possible  limited
impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Localized rainfall flooding may prompt a few evacuations.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly rise with swifter currents.
Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may become swollen
and overflow in spots.
- Flood waters can enter a few structures, especially in usually
vulnerable spots. A few places where rapid ponding of water
occurs at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Several storm drains and retention ponds become
near-full and begin to overflow. Some brief road and bridge
closures.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* OTHER COASTAL HAZARDS:
There will be a high risk of rip currents across the upper Texas
coastal beaches through Friday.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Keep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose
power, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and
check-ins.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Houston/Galveston TX around 7 PM CDT, or sooner if
conditions warrant.

This product covers Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas

**TROPICAL STORM BERTHA HAS MOVED INLAND INTO SOUTHEASTERN TEXAS.**


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- The Tropical Storm Warning has been cancelled for Lower Iberia,
Lower St. Mary, and Lower Vermilion

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for East Cameron, Lower
Jefferson, and West Cameron

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 30 miles northwest of High Island TX or about 80 miles
west of Cameron LA
- 29.8N 94.7W
- Storm Intensity 40 mph
- Movement West-northwest or 290 degrees at 13 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Bertha has moved inland over lower Southeast Texas
continuing a weakening trend. Tropical storm warnings have been
discontinued east of the Cameron / Vermilion Parish line as well as
marine south extending south and east of Calcasieu Pass. Tropical
Storm Warnings remain in effect across western Cameron Parish,
Louisiana, and Jefferson County, Texas including Calcasieu and Sabine
Lakes. The remainder of the forecast remains unchanged with 1 to
2 feet of surge possible and most of the heavy rainfall remaining
offshore due to the sheared nature of the convection. Bertha is
expected to weaken into a tropical depression overnight as it
encounters more land interaction moving further into Texas.


POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
Southwest Louisiana / Southeast Texas. Remain well sheltered from hazardous
wind having limited impacts. If realized,
these impacts include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Potential impacts from the main surge event are now unfolding across
Southwest Louisiana / Southeast Texas. Remain well away from locally hazardous
surge having limited impacts. If
realized, these impacts include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time
across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas.

* TORNADOES:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time
across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:

Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Now is the time to stay inside and away from windows. Listen for
updates and be ready in case you lose electrical power. Keep a
battery-powered radio, charged cell phone and flashlight handy.

During the peak of the storm be ready to move quickly. Keep your
shoes on and rain gear handy. Boots and athletic shoes offer the best
foot protection if you become unexpectedly exposed to the weather.

Keep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose
power, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and
check-ins.



* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Lake Charles LA around 10 PM CDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

Storm Warnings remain in effect across western Cameron Parish,
Louisiana, and Jefferson County, Texas including Calcasieu and Sabine

2 feet of surge possible and most of the heavy rainfall remaining
offshore due to the sheared nature of the convection. Bertha is
expected to weaken into a tropical depression overnight as it
encounters more land interaction moving further into Texas.

Southwest Louisiana / Southeast Texas. Remain well sheltered from hazardous

Southwest Louisiana / Southeast Texas. Remain well away from locally hazardous
surge having limited impacts. If
realized, these impacts include:

immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

battery-powered radio, charged cell phone and flashlight handy.

shoes on and rain gear handy. Boots and athletic shoes offer the best
foot protection if you become unexpectedly exposed to the weather.

alerts.description:
HLSHGX

This product covers Southeast Texas

**Bertha Weakens to a Depression, All Tropical Storm Warnings are Cancelled**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- All watches and warnings have been canceled

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 20 miles north-northeast of Houston TX
- 29.9N 95.3W
- Storm Intensity 35 mph
- Movement West or 280 degrees at 13 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Depression Bertha continues to weaken as it moves westward
through southeast Texas. Bertha will continue to weaken, becoming a
post-tropical system as it moves westward tonight. Locally heavy
downpours remain possible for the next few hours mainly to the south
and southwest of the center. No other significant impacts are expected
as winds continue to subside.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Additional impacts from flooding rain are still a concern across the
western Houston metro and Brazos Valley. Remain well guarded against
locally hazardous flood waters having further impacts of limited
potential.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Be alert for flooded roads. Do not drive through places where flood
waters cover the road. Turn around, don't drown!

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

As it pertains to this event...this will be the last local statement
issued by the National Weather Service in Houston/Galveston TX
regarding the effects of tropical cyclone hazards upon the area.

alerts.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued July 23 at 4:15PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
alerts.description:
HLSHGX

This product covers Southeast Texas

**Bertha expected to weaken as it moves through Southeast Texas**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Bolivar Peninsula,
Brazoria Islands, Chambers, Coastal Brazoria, Coastal
Galveston, and Galveston Island

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 40 miles north of Galveston TX
- 29.8N 94.7W
- Storm Intensity 40 mph
- Movement West-northwest or 290 degrees at 13 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Bertha is currently moving westward through southeast
Texas, roughtly around the I-10 corridor nearly Galveston bay. It's
intensity has decreased, with peak winds upwards of 35 knots. Bertha
will continue to weaken, becoming a post-tropical system as it moves
westward tonight. No significant impacts to Southeast Texas are
expected at this time. Winds of 15-25 knots with gusts to 35 knots will
be possible, mainly along the coast and Gulf waters. Scattered showers
and thunderstorms continue this evening. Heavy downpours are possible
though the flooding rain threat is very low. A high risk rip currents
will continue across the beaches and coast through Friday.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
Southeast Texas. Remain well sheltered from hazardous wind having
possible limited impacts. If realized, these impacts
include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across
the Southeast Texas coast. Remain well guarded against locally
hazardous flood waters having possible  limited
impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Localized rainfall flooding may prompt a few evacuations.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly rise with swifter currents.
Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may become swollen
and overflow in spots.
- Flood waters can enter a few structures, especially in usually
vulnerable spots. A few places where rapid ponding of water
occurs at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Several storm drains and retention ponds become
near-full and begin to overflow. Some brief road and bridge
closures.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* OTHER COASTAL HAZARDS:
There will be a high risk of rip currents across the upper Texas
coastal beaches through Friday.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Keep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose
power, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and
check-ins.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Houston/Galveston TX around 7 PM CDT, or sooner if
conditions warrant.
